reference_products.name: Boxed Mac software: MacWrite/MacPaint 'Guided Tour' + manuals (1984)

information_architecture_patterns.label: Nav = Product · Docs · Pricing (+ GitHub, Download, primary buy)
information_architecture_patterns.one_line: Every peer that sells something exposes a literal 'Pricing' link (Paper, pen.dev, tldraw, Raycast, Penpot); pen.dev runs on just Downloads/Pricing/Docs. Changelog/roadmap/blog sit in the body teaser or footer.

information_architecture_patterns.label: Hero → product shot → proof → 3–4 chapters → pricing band → changelog teaser → closing CTA
information_architecture_patterns.one_line: Linear's order; Paper, Framer and Craft vary only the chapter count. Proof sits right under the shot, never at the bottom.

information_architecture_patterns.label: Free local app + one paid hosted plan + contact-us tier
information_architecture_patterns.one_line: The free thing is a real product ('Free without limits', '$0 forever'), the paid thing is hosting/sync, and the unit is explained in one sentence.

information_architecture_patterns.label: Docs landing with two doors: Using (tutorials/how-to) and Advanced (reference/explanation)
information_architecture_patterns.one_line: Raycast splits Manual from Developers; Stripe leads with no-code use cases before product reference; Diátaxis gives each door its modes. Heritage: Guided Tour + reference manual in one box.

information_architecture_patterns.label: 'Maude vs Figma' comparison as a footer-linked page, not a hero argument
information_architecture_patterns.one_line: Paper and pen.dev keep the Figma comparison out of the hero (Paper: footer 'Paper vs Figma'); third-party comparisons that admit 'where Figma still wins' read as more credible.

regions.purpose: One release line ('Maude 2 is here — see what's new →') that replaces a top-level What's new link.
regions.size: 1 line, centered above H1 or as a pill inside the nav row

regions.purpose: Brand + 3 links + GitHub + Download (ghost) + Get Maude Cloud (primary); condenses on scroll.
Three-line headline ('You like Figma. / You like Claude. / Meet Maude.'), one-sentence lede, two CTAs, one fine-print price line.
The app window with AI drawing on an artboard — the proof that it is a real canvas; plays the intro demo once.
regions.size: full content width, ~560–640px tall, overlapping the hero bottom

regions.purpose: Honest proof for a new indie product: GitHub stars, MIT, no telemetry, releases count, made in Brno — not fake logos.
3 tiles: draw or ask, design system checks, share and talk.
'Feels like Figma. Lives in your files.' — files, GitHub copy, export, self-host.
Buy Maude Cloud: per-project price, what's included, primary CTA + see pricing.
'Live in a terminal? It's all still here.' plugins/CLI/hub with install lines.
3 latest releases, 'View all' — the changelog's new home.
Product · Docs · Project · Legal columns incl. Changelog, Roadmap, vs Figma, coffee.

interaction_patterns.label: Product shot plays a short scripted AI run once
interaction_patterns.rationale: Framer's typed prompt → 'Thinking…' → result and Paper's live-canvas visual show the product instead of describing it; for Maude it proves 'AI draws on the artboard while you watch'.

interaction_patterns.label: Per-seat vs per-project cost bars for a 5-person team
interaction_patterns.rationale: Figma needs a seat-type matrix and a 'what is a seat' FAQ; one bar chart beats that explanation. Animate the bars growing once in view (motion carries data).

interaction_patterns.label: One-line 'Your Claude account is separate' callout on pricing
interaction_patterns.rationale: Zed explains own-key AI right on the pricing page; prevents the 'is AI included?' bounce.

interaction_patterns.label: ⌘K search + Ask AI + Copy page as Markdown on docs
interaction_patterns.rationale: Supabase puts search + Ask AI in the docs top bar; Stripe ships .md twins. For an AI-native tool, docs readable by Claude are a feature.

interaction_patterns.label: Nav island shrinks and frosts after the hero
interaction_patterns.rationale: maude-v2's own signature (floating islands); keeps the buy CTA reachable without a heavy sticky bar.

anti_patterns.pattern: Mega-menus with 15+ links (Penpot: 18 under three menus; STUDIO: 7 menus; Framer: 94 nav links)
anti_patterns.why: The brief asks for simpler navigation; Maude has one product and one paid plan — nothing to mega-menu.

anti_patterns.pattern: Logo wall of companies that don't use the product
anti_patterns.why: A new indie tool's credibility comes from honest proof (GitHub, MIT, no telemetry, changelog cadence), as tldraw and Plausible do; borrowed logos read as fake.

anti_patterns.pattern: Seat-type matrices and AI-credit meters on the pricing page
anti_patterns.why: Figma needs 4 plans × 3 seat types × credits; Maude's whole pricing argument is that it doesn't.
Award-site staples (Lusion, Active Theory) that hurt a pro tool's clarity and trigger vestibular issues; reduced-motion guidance says scroll-driven motion should disappear, not just shorten.

anti_patterns.pattern: Figma comparison in the H1 as a claim ('Figma killer')
anti_patterns.why: Peers avoid it (Paper, pen.dev keep 'vs Figma' in the footer); the brief's 'You like Figma. You like Claude.' is an invitation, not an attack — keep it that way.

current_trends.trend: Agent-readable sites: docs .md twins, llms.txt, 'Read in your terminal', a note to agents at the top of the homepage
MCP / 'works with Claude, Codex, Cursor' sections on design-tool homepages

motion_patterns.label: Headline lines arrive one by one, the last lands with the spark
motion_patterns.where: Hero H1 ('You like Figma.' / 'You like Claude.' / 'Meet Maude.')
motion_patterns.why_it_works: The headline is literally a three-beat joke; staging the beats makes the punchline land. Plays once on load, done before the eye reaches the CTAs.
motion_patterns.duration_easing: each line opacity 0→1 + translateY 8px→0 over var(--dur-route) 280ms, var(--ease-out); stagger 90ms; 'Meet Maude.' starts at ~360ms and the spark glyph scales 0.6→1 on var(--ease-spring) 420ms. Total < 900ms. Lede + CTAs fade in at 500ms, 160ms.
motion_patterns.reduced_motion: Everything rendered in its final state at first paint; no transform, no fade.
motion_patterns.evidence: School of Motion 2026 roundup: 'motion should support the content rather than compete'; Apple gives single messages their own moment.

motion_patterns.label: The product shot plays one scripted AI run
motion_patterns.why_it_works: Shows the core promise — select, ask, watch the AI draw — in 4–5 s. Framer's hero uses the same prompt → Thinking → result beat.
motion_patterns.duration_easing: Sequence starts when 40% visible: prompt types in the AI panel (≈35 ms/char, ~1.2 s) → spark cursor glides to the Pricing artboard (600 ms var(--ease-in-out)) → 3 pricing cards draw skeleton→filled with 120 ms stagger (var(--dur-panel) each) → 'AI is drawing' chip swaps to 'Done' + Tereza's sticky lands with var(--ease-spring). Plays once; a small Replay button (≥44px hit) appears after.
motion_patterns.reduced_motion: Show the final frame (cards drawn, sticky placed, chat complete) with no cursor travel; Replay hidden.
motion_patterns.evidence: Framer hero typed prompt demo; Paper's canvas visual with collaborator cursors.

motion_patterns.label: Quiet reveal of sections on scroll
motion_patterns.where: Section heads and card groups below the fold
motion_patterns.why_it_works: Gives rhythm without performing; marks progress through the page.
motion_patterns.duration_easing: CSS animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% entry 30%; opacity 0→1 + translateY 12px; card stagger via --i * 60ms delay. Wrap in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and @supports (animation-timeline: view()).
motion_patterns.reduced_motion: Static; content visible by default (motion is opt-in, never hide-then-reveal under reduce or no-support).
motion_patterns.evidence: Reduced-motion guidance: scroll-driven motion must disappear, default static, opt in via no-preference; keep to transform/opacity.

motion_patterns.label: Canvas + AI = Maude cards assemble
motion_patterns.why_it_works: The '+' and '=' are the argument; letting the third card arrive after the two inputs reads as an equation solving.
motion_patterns.duration_easing: Cards 1 and 2 reveal together (280ms ease-out), '+' then '=' fade (160ms), Maude card rises last with var(--ease-spring) 420ms — triggered once at entry 25%.

motion_patterns.label: Pricing comparison bars grow to their value
motion_patterns.where: Cloud page 'Per project, never per seat' cost chart
motion_patterns.why_it_works: Motion that carries data: the per-seat bar visibly keeps growing past Maude's — the whole pricing argument in one second.
motion_patterns.duration_easing: scaleX 0→1 from left over 600ms var(--ease-out), 80ms stagger; numbers count-up optional (no, keep static numbers for AT).
motion_patterns.reduced_motion: Bars at full width, no transition.
motion_patterns.evidence: Figma pricing needs a seat matrix; one animated comparison replaces it.

motion_patterns.label: Nav island condenses after the hero
motion_patterns.why_it_works: maude-v2's signature shape — chrome floats and folds; keeps 'Get Maude Cloud' in reach.
motion_patterns.duration_easing: padding/height + backdrop to --island-bg over var(--dur-panel) 220ms var(--ease-out), triggered by scroll() past 120px (or IntersectionObserver on the hero sentinel).
motion_patterns.evidence: maude-v2 README: islands fold into an icon; Ableton keeps 'Try free' persistently in the header.

motion_patterns.label: Hover/press on cards, doors, buttons
motion_patterns.why_it_works: Feedback within one frame; signals clickability on large card targets.
motion_patterns.duration_easing: var(--dur-flip) 120ms, translateY -2px + shadow step; press scale .98.
motion_patterns.evidence: Kowalski-derived guidance: UI transitions ~200ms ease-out; never animate keyboard-initiated actions.

value._motion_rules: Total intro budget under ~1 s for text, ~5 s for the one product demo; animate only transform/opacity; one spring moment per viewport (spark, sticky landing, Maude card) per DS rule 'spring only for playful moments'; never loop forever; no smooth-scroll library, no scroll-jacking, no parallax; content is visible without JS and without animation-timeline support.
